mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% over three consecutive months indicates labor market deterioration, which precedes negative S&P 500 returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signal broad demand weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases (i.e., returns positive >55% of times when both decline).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 95.0 indicates manufacturing sector weakness, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during industrial contraction regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO remains below 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: Rising residential construction permits (HOUST) signal housing market strength, which typically boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, which typically triggers monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal severe labor market deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases (i.e., returns positive >55% of times when both conditions hold).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate above 8.5% during recessionary labor market regimes typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.5%.
